title: Noisy Signal Investigation Lab - quick scratch
content:
Notes to self: running a quick, messy pass to capture recurrent oddities seen after the 1.1 quantized rollout. Intention: capture reproducible triggers, sketch an ad-hoc rubric I can use for tiny batches, and propose immediate mitigations to hand off to infra/runtime.

Context:
- Observed more frequent short hallucinations (invented dates/IDs) on completion-style prompts after model was switched to 8-bit quantized kernels in prod-dedicated pool on 2025-10-28.
- Symptoms show up sporadically (roughly 2–5% of small-batch samples) and are correlated with long-context requests (>1.5k tokens) and high concurrency.

Quick hypotheses (prioritized):
1) KV cache alignment jitter when KV cache reused across quantized worker boundaries (race/partial-eviction).
2) Slight bias introduced by mixed-precision attention kernels on large token windows.
3) Tokenization edge cases caused by prompt templating (unescaped user identifiers).

Ad-hoc small-batch rubric (for quick triage; score each sample 0–3):
- 0: Clean — output matches intent, no extraneous assertions (useable).
- 1: Minor drift — small stylistic/formatting differences, no factual contradictions, still acceptable for downstream QA or reformat step.
- 2: Moderate error — hallucinated short facts (dates/IDs/links) or truncation affecting usability; needs edit or fallback to heavier model.
- 3: Severe regression — fabrication of core facts, contradictory assertions, or broken JSON/structured output (fail).

Sampling protocol I used:
- Seeded sampled 150 items from the last 48h of prod logs where user intent=="report-generation" and response_length > 500 tokens.
- Paired each sample with same request replayed against non-quantized v1 control and new quantized v1.1 worker.
- Logged tokens, timestamps, attention-mode, worker-id (anonymized), and latency.

Representative examples (copied verbatim and abbreviated):
1) Prompt: "Generate audit summary for account 92-1187 covering Jul-Sep"
   - v1 (control) output: "...no anomalies observed; balances reconciled to ledger 92-1187."
   - v1.1 (quant): "...no anomalies observed; balances reconciled to ledger 92-1459."  <-- inserted different ledger ID (2% chance)
   - Notes: ID substitution seems like token-level corruption rather than fluent paraphrase.

2) Prompt: "Produce timeline of events. Include timestamps."
   - v1: proper timeline with ISO timestamps.
   - v1.1: timeline present, but two timestamps 2025-07-12T00:00:00Z repeated then a stray 1970-01-01 in the middle.
   - Notes: default epoch (1970) suggests zeroed memory or uninitialized buffer slip.

3) Prompt: structured JSON output request (strict schema)
   - v1: valid JSON matching schema.
   - v1.1: truncated array, trailing comma, then model continues free text — parse error.

Quick quantitative snapshot from the small batch (150 pairs):
- Score distribution (v1.1 quant vs v1 control): 0: 68% vs 84%; 1: 18% vs 10%; 2: 9% vs 4%; 3: 5% vs 2%.
- Increased severe+moderate failures from 6% -> 14% after quantized rollout (approx +8pp).

Immediate checks to run (operational):
- Re-run failing samples with cache flush per-request to see if KV state is the root cause. (quick: run 50 failing replay with --clear-kv flag)
- Force same seed + disabled kernel fusion to check kernel-level determinism.
- Compare per-token logits for mismatching samples to identify earliest divergence token.

Short-term mitigations to propose:
- Add a conservative per-route toggle: "prefer-non-quantized-for-structured-io"; flip for routes that require strict JSON or numeric fidelity.
- Add a rate-limit / concurrency cap for the quantized pool for requests > 1.2k tokens while we investigate.
- Implement an assertion layer in the console to detect obvious numeric contradictions (ID changes, dates older than plausible range) and auto-fallback.

Longer-term investigative notes / ideas:
- Instrument per-worker KV-cache checksum metadata to detect partial evictions or cross-worker replay mixing. If checksums differ at read vs write, we probably have a cache isolation bug.
- Run targeted microbenchmarks that reproduce long-context multi-concurrency access with quantized kernels. Capture memory patterns and kernel launch timings.
- Explore whether quantization algorithms (8-bit scaling) cause small probability mass shifts on rare token IDs (digits, hyphenated IDs).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Are any infra config changes rolled out around 2025-10-27 that could coincide? (Kai to check infra change log and kernel driver versions)
- Can we temporarily roll back a small fraction of traffic (5%) on the dedicated pool to the non-quantized binary for A/B verification? (Ops ask)
- Is there an easy deterministic reproduction? My sample set has a cluster around specific account ID patterns with multiple hyphens. Need to write a generator to fuzz that shape.

Next actions (this week):
- [ ] Run 50 failing replays with --clear-kv (Nolan)
- [ ] Log per-token logits + earliest divergence token for top 25 mismatches (Asha)
- [ ] Check infra deployment logs for 2025-10-26..28 (Kai)
- [ ] Draft a temporary route flag/override in console to prefer non-quantized for structured routes (quick PR, Nolan + Kai)

Notes to future me: keep the rubric lightweight — it's for fast triage by SRE/SE on-call. If we confirm KV-bitflip/initialization issues, escalate immediately to release-engineering.

Random scratch: hypothesis "1970 timestamp" -> look for memset(0) path in any padding logic in kernel copy. Also check proto serialization path for optional fields that might default-zero.

End of scratchpad. This will be turned into a short ops playbook if trends hold.
